subject: Democratic Republic of the Congo
note: Cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary): Congo River, using only its figures. The page says the river is the world's deepest recorded river, with measured depths of around 220 m, and also 'greater than 220 m'; the episode says only 'around 220 m' and credits the page. The page gives two lengths: 4,700 km for the whole Congo-Lualaba-Luvua-Luapula-Chambeshi system (ninth-longest in the world) and 4,370 km for the Congo with the Lualaba; the episode uses only 4,370 km. Discharge uses the page's average at the mouth (41,000 m3/s); the page also gives a figure of 41,860 m3/s and a range, which are not used. Depth is NOT computed from any elevation grid (rivers are far below its resolution). The river is drawn from the pinned Natural Earth rivers layer, and Kinshasa and Brazzaville are map-data cities. Frames stay on the river, with no highlight of disputed areas.

claims.text: The Congo River is the world's deepest recorded river, with measured depths of around 220 m (720 ft).
The Congo River is the second-longest river in Africa, shorter only than the Nile, and the third largest river in the world by discharge volume, following the Amazon and the Ganges-Brahmaputra.
Measured along with the Lualaba, the Congo River has a total length of 4,370 km (2,720 mi).
The Congo is the only major river to cross the equator twice.
The Congo's discharge at its mouth ranges from 23,000 to 75,000 m3/s, with an average of 41,000 m3/s.
Because its drainage basin includes areas both north and south of the Equator, its flow is stable, as there is always at least one part of the river experiencing a rainy season.
The Livingstone Falls are a series of 32 falls and rapids with an elevation change of 270 metres over 350 kilometres.
Kinshasa and Brazzaville are on opposite sides of the river at the Pool (Pool Malebo), where the river narrows and falls through a number of cataracts in deep canyons.
The Congo basin covers ten countries and accounts for about 13% of Africa.
The Congo's drainage basin covers 4,014,500 km2, an area nearly equal to that of the European Union.
